column3: The Hebrew begins with “behold, they will not believe me,” rather than an explicit “What if” question.
The Hebrew says “in your bosom” where BSB has “inside your cloak”; “white” is supplied.
The signs have a “voice,” rendered “witness” in BSB.
The Hebrew calls him “heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue,” and names “yesterday” and “the day before.”
“I will be with your mouth” preserves the image rendered “I will help you as you speak.”
The Hebrew says “send by the hand of whom You will send,” without an explicit “someone else.”
“With your mouth and with his mouth” preserves the repeated image rendered “help both of you to speak.”
The Hebrew calls Aaron “a mouth” rather than “your spokesman.”
The Hebrew says “in your hand” where BSB has “within your power.”
The object is only “him,” without an explicit name Moses.
The Hebrew says “his feet,” without an explicit name Moses.
“Circumcisions” is plural; the subject who withdraws remains unnamed.
The Hebrew has “he performed the signs,” without explicitly repeating Moses’ name.
